verses.zh: （大卫的诗。）耶和华啊，我的心仰望你。
verses.en: By David.O Lord, I come before you in prayer.[NOTE:1]
notes: Psalm 25. The psalmist asks for divine protection, guidance and forgiveness as he affirms his loyalty to and trust in the Lord. This psalm is an acrostic; every verse begins with a successive letter of the Hebrew alphabet, except for v. 18, which, like v. 19, begins with ר (resh) instead of the expected ק (qof). The final verse, which begins with פ (pe), stands outside the acrostic scheme.

verses.zh: 我的　神啊，我素来倚靠你；求你不要叫我羞愧，不要叫我的仇敌向我夸胜。
verses.en: My God, I trust in you.Please do not let me be humiliated;do not let my enemies triumphantly rejoice over me.

verses.zh: 凡等候你的必不羞愧；惟有那无故行奸诈的必要羞愧。
verses.en: Certainly none who rely on you will be humiliated.Those who deal in treachery will be thwarted[NOTE:1] and humiliated.
notes: Heb “to you, O Lord, my life I lift up.” To “lift up” one’s “life” to the Lord means to express one’s trust in him through prayer. See Pss 86:4; 143:8.

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，求你将你的道指示我，将你的路教训我！
verses.en: Make me understand your ways, O Lord.Teach me your paths.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “those who deal in treachery in vain.” The adverb רֵיקָם (reqam, “in vain”) probably refers to the failure (or futility) of their efforts. Another option is to understand it as meaning “without cause” (cf. NIV84 “without excuse”; NIV11 “without cause”; NRSV “wantonly treacherous”).

verses.zh: 求你以你的真理引导我，教训我，因为你是救我的　神。我终日等候你。
verses.en: Guide me into your truth[NOTE:1] and teach me.For you are the God who delivers me;on you I rely all day long.
notes: Teach me your paths. In this context the Lord’s “ways” and “paths” refer to the moral principles which the Lord prescribes for his followers. See vv. 8-10.

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，求你记念你的怜悯和慈爱，因为这是亘古以来所常有的。
verses.en: Remember[NOTE:1] your compassionate and faithful deeds, O Lord,for you have always acted in this manner.[NOTE:2]
notes: The Lord’s commandments are referred to as truth here because they are a trustworthy and accurate expression of the divine will.
That is, “remember” with the intention of repeating.

verses.zh: 求你不要记念我幼年的罪愆和我的过犯；耶和华啊，求你因你的恩惠，按你的慈爱记念我。
verses.en: Do not hold against me[NOTE:1] the sins of my youth[NOTE:2] or my rebellious acts.Because you are faithful to me, extend to me your favor, O Lord.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “for from antiquity [are] they.”
Heb “do not remember,” with the intention of punishing.
That is, the sins characteristic of youths, who lack moral discretion and wisdom.

verses.zh: 耶和华是良善正直的，所以他必指示罪人走正路。
verses.en: The Lord is both kind and fair;[NOTE:1] that is why he teaches sinners the right way to live.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “according to your faithfulness, remember me, you, for the sake of your goodness, O Lord.”
Heb “good and just.”

verses.zh: 他必按公平引领谦卑人，将他的道教训他们。
verses.en: May he show[NOTE:1] the humble what is right.[NOTE:2] May he teach[NOTE:3] the humble his way.
notes: Heb “teaches sinners in the way.”
The prefixed verbal form is jussive; the psalmist expresses his prayer.

Heb “may he guide the humble into justice.” The Hebrew term עֲנָוִים (ʿanavim, “humble”) usually refers to the oppressed, but in this context, where the psalmist confesses his sin and asks for moral guidance, it apparently refers to sinners who humble themselves before God and seek deliverance from their sinful condition.

verses.zh: 凡遵守他的约和他法度的人，耶和华都以慈爱诚实待他。
verses.en: The Lord always proves faithful and reliable[NOTE:1] to those who follow the demands of his covenant.[NOTE:2]
notes: The prefixed verbal form is interpreted as a jussive (it stands parallel to the jussive form, “may he guide”).
Heb “all the paths of the Lord are faithful and trustworthy.” The Lord’s “paths” refer here to his characteristic actions.

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，求你因你的名赦免我的罪，因为我的罪重大。
verses.en: For the sake of your reputation,[NOTE:1] O Lord,forgive my sin, because it is great.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “to the ones who keep his covenant and his testimonies.”
Heb “name.” By forgiving the sinful psalmist, the Lord’s reputation as a merciful God will be enhanced.

verses.zh: 谁敬畏耶和华，耶和华必指示他当选择的道路。
verses.en: The Lord shows his faithful followersthe way they should live.[NOTE:1]
notes: Forgive my sin because it is great. The psalmist readily admits his desperate need for forgiveness.

verses.zh: 他必安然居住；他的后裔必承受地土。
verses.en: They experience his favor;[NOTE:1] their descendants[NOTE:2] inherit the land.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “Who is this man, the one who fears the Lord? He will instruct him in the way he should choose.” The singular (note “man”) is representative here (see v. 14, where the plural is used), and has thus been translated as a plural (“followers…they”).
Heb “his life in goodness dwells.” The singular is representative (see v. 14).
Or “offspring”; Heb “seed.”

verses.zh: 耶和华与敬畏他的人亲密；他必将自己的约指示他们。
verses.en: The Lord’s loyal followers receive his guidance,[NOTE:1] and he reveals his covenantal demands to them.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “earth.”
Heb “the advice of the Lord belongs to those who fear him.”

verses.zh: 我的眼目时常仰望耶和华，因为他必将我的脚从网里拉出来。
verses.en: I continually look to the Lord for help,[NOTE:1] for he will free my feet from the enemy’s net.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and his covenant, to make them know.”
Heb “my eyes continually [are] toward the Lord.”

verses.zh: 求你转向我，怜恤我，因为我是孤独困苦。
verses.en: Turn toward me and have mercy on me,for I am alone[NOTE:1] and oppressed.
notes: Heb “for he will bring out from a net my feet.” The hostility of the psalmist’s enemies is probably in view (see v. 19).

verses.zh: 我心里的愁苦甚多，求你救我脱离我的祸患。
verses.en: Deliver me from my distress;[NOTE:1] rescue me from my suffering.[NOTE:2]
notes: That is, helpless and vulnerable.

Heb “the distresses of my heart, they make wide.” The text makes little if any sense as it stands, unless this is an otherwise unattested intransitive use of the Hiphil of רָחַב (rakhav, “be wide”). It is preferable to emend the form הִרְחִיבוּ (hirkhivu; Hiphil perfect third plural “they make wide”) to הַרְחֵיב (harkhev; Hiphil imperative masculine singular “make wide”). (The final vav [ו] can be joined to the following word and taken as a conjunction.) In this case one can translate, “[in/from] the distresses of my heart, make wide [a place for me],” that is, “deliver me from the distress I am experiencing.” For the expression “make wide [a place for me],” see Ps 4:1.

verses.zh: 求你看顾我的困苦，我的艰难，赦免我一切的罪。
verses.en: See my pain and suffering.Forgive all my sins.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “from my distresses lead me out.”

verses.zh: 求你察看我的仇敌，因为他们人多，并且痛痛地恨我。
verses.en: Watch my enemies, for they outnumber me;they hate me and want to harm me.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “lift up all my sins.”

verses.zh: 求你保护我的性命，搭救我，使我不致羞愧，因为我投靠你。
verses.en: Protect me[NOTE:1] and deliver me!Please do not let me be humiliated,for I have taken shelter in you.
notes: Heb “see my enemies for they are numerous, and [with] violent hatred they hate me.”

verses.zh: 愿纯全、正直保守我，因为我等候你。
verses.en: May integrity and godliness protect me,for I rely on you.

verses.zh: 神啊，求你救赎以色列脱离他一切的愁苦。
verses.en: O God, rescue[NOTE:1] Israelfrom all their distress![NOTE:2]
notes: Or “my life.”
Or “redeem.”

READING CYCLE THREE (see
"Bible
Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- This is an acrostic (cf. NJB's strophes). However, two letters are missing and two are
doubled (Jewish Study Bible, p. 1309).

- It is dominated by emphatic prayer requests.

- COHORTATIVES

- Ps. 25:2 – "do not let me be ashamed," BDB 101, KB 116,
Qal COHORTATIVE (this root is used four times in this
Psalm; it is not so much embarrassment as it is the exposure of faithlessness)

- Ps. 25:20 – "do not let me be ashamed, same as a., but Qal
IMPERFECT used in a COHORTATIVE sense (inclusio)

- IMPERFECTS used in a JUSSIVE sense

- Ps. 25:2 – "do not let my enemies exult over me," BDB 763, KB 836,
Qal IMPERFECT

- Ps. 25:7 – "do not remember the sins," BDB 269, KB 269, Qal
IMPERFECT (this root is used three times in Ps. 25:6-7)

- Ps. 25:21 – "let integrity and uprightness preserve me," BDB 665,
KB 718, Qal IMPERFECT

- IMPERATIVES

- Ps. 25:4 – "make me know Your Ways," BDB 393, KB 390, Hiphil

- Ps. 25:4 – "teach me Your paths," BDB 540, KB 531, Piel

- Ps. 25:5 – "lead me in Your truth," BDB 201, KB 231, Hiphil

- Ps. 25:5 – "teach me," same as b.

- Ps. 25:6 – "remember," BDB 269, KB 268, Qal

- Ps. 25:7 – "remember," same as e.

- Ps. 25:16 – "turn to me," BDB 815, KB 937, Qal

- Ps. 25:16 – "be gracious to me," BDB 335, KB 334, Qal

- Ps. 25:17 – "bring me out of my distress," BDB 422, KB 425,
Hiphil

- Ps. 25:18 – "look upon my affliction," BDB 906, KB1157, Qal

- Ps. 25:18 – "forgive all my sin," BDB 669, KB 1157, Qal

- Ps. 25:19 – "look upon my enemies," same as j.

- Ps. 25:20 – "guard my soul," BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal

- Ps. 25:20 – "deliver me," BDB 664, KB 717, Hiphil

- Ps. 25:22 – "redeem Israel," BDB 804, KB 911, Qal

- Many of the Psalms in Book 1 (Psalm 1-41) deal with issues related to

- Israel's battles with the surrounding nations

- the Davidic King's

- prayers for victory

- praises for victory

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: PSALM 25:1-3
1To
You, O Lord, I lift up my soul.
2O my God, in You I
trust,
Do not let me be
ashamed;
Do not let my
enemies exult over me.
3Indeed,
none of those who wait for You will be ashamed;
Those who deal treacherously without
cause will be ashamed.

25:1-3 The psalmist fears being ashamed by his enemies but in the midst of his fear he
expresses his faith in YHWH's promised victory.

He characterizes himself as one who

- lifts his soul to YHWH – BDB 669, KB 724, Qal IMPERFECT, which
denotes continual action (cf. Ps. 86:4; 143:8)

- trusts in YHWH – BDB 105, KB 120, Qal PERFECT, which denotes
a settled action/condition. It is used often in Psalms (example from Book 1 of of Ps. 9:10; 21:7; 22:4,5;
25:2; 26:1; 28:7; 32:10; 37:3; 40:4)

- waits for YHWH – BDB 875, KB 1082, Qal PARTICIPLE
(cf. Ps. 27:14; 37:34; 39:7; 52:9, AB, p. 155)
suggests it is from another root with the same letters that means "to call" or
"to invoke"

Because of this he is confident that he will not be

- ashamed (inclusio, cf. Ps. 25:20; 31:1; see

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHAME)

- exulted over (cf. Ps. 41:11)

but that his enemies will be (cf. Ps. 25:3b). In a sense those who
trust in YHWH are witnesses of His character. How they live and trust gives powerful
evidence of the reality and character of YHWH.

SPECIAL
TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

25:1 "O Lord" This is the title of Israel's Covenant God, YHWH. It
is first used in Gen. 2:4 and is a form of the Hebrew VERB "to be."

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣ "soul" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: NEPHESH

▣ "O God" This is the SINGULAR form of Elohim, the title for Israel's
God as Creator, Provider, and Sustainer of all life on this planet.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C.

25:3

NASB, NKJV, NRSV, REB

This ADJECTIVE (BDB 938, KB 1229) can be understood in two ways.

- without cause (cf. Ps. 7:4)

- to no effect (cf. Isa. 55:11; Jer. 50:9)

me know Your ways, O Lord;
Teach me Your paths.
5Lead me in Your truth
and teach me,
For You are
the God of my salvation;
For

O Lord, Your compassion and Your
lovingkindnesses,
For they
have been from of old.
7Do

According to Your lovingkindness
remember me,
For Your
goodness' sake, O Lord.

25:4-7 Notice the string of powerful emphatic IMPERATIVES which requests YHWH's
action on behalf of the one who trusts in Him.

- know (BDB 393, KB 390, Hiphil IMPERATIVE) His ways (BDB 202,
cf. Ps. 25:4,8,9,12; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY)

- teach (BDB 540, KB 531, Piel IMPERATIVE) him His paths (BDB 73,
cf. Ps. 25:4,10)

- lead (BDB 201, KB 231, Hiphil IMPERATIVE) him in His truth (BDB 54,
see
SPECIAL
TOPIC: Believe, Trust, Faith, and Faithfulness in the Old Testament)

- teach (BDB 540, KB 531, Piel IMPERATIVE) me

The one who trusts (and waits, Ps. 25:5c, 21b) wants to know YHWH in both personal fellowship
and revelatory truth. Based on this truth and lifestyle obedience, he then requests that YHWH

- remember His character (cf. Ps. 25:7b,c), see
SPECIAL
TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

- compassion ‒ BDB 933 (Ps. 25:5)

- lovingkindness ‒ BDB 338 (cf. Ps. 25:6,7), see
SPECIAL
TOPIC: LOVINGKINDNESS

- goodness ‒ BDB 375 (Ps. 25:7)

- do not remember the sins (BDB 308) of his youth (cf. Job 13:26)

- do not remember his transgressions (BDB 833)

24:4 "ways. . .paths" The revelatory truths of YHWH were viewed as a well marked/worn
road or trail (see note at Ps. 1:1). There was no confusion about what to do, only the need for obedience
to the well-marked path (cf. Ps. 139:24). God's path is often described as level, straight, unobstructed,
clearly visible.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

24:6 "For they have been from of old" The psalmist is asking YHWH to act towards him
(and Israel, cf. Ps. 25:22) in the consistent ways that He has displayed in the past (cf. Ps. 89:49).
In essence the psalmist wants the covenant God to remember His covenant promises. He has acted in the
past, now please act again for Your people and purposes. Even though the psalmist and Israel have
sinned foolishly, please let Your covenant love (hesed, i.e., covenant loyalty) and Your basic
character (i.e., goodness and mercy, cf. Ps. 23:6), forgive the humble sinner (cf. Ps. 25:8-11).

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVVENANT

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: PSALM 25:8-11
8Good
and upright is the Lord;
Therefore
He instructs sinners in the way.
9He
leads the humble in justice,
And
He teaches the humble His way.
10All
the paths of the Lord are lovingkindness and truth
To those who keep His covenant and
His testimonies.
11For
Your name's sake, O Lord,
Pardon my iniquity, for it is great.

25:8-11 Many of the key words and concepts from Ps. 25:4-7 are repeated in this strophe. Remember
this is an acrostic psalm. All of the psalmist's poetic license and creativity are being used.

- Ps. 25:8a extols YHWH's character, as did Ps. 25:6,7

- good (BDB 373)

- upright (BDB 449)

- Ps. 25:8b-9 again mention YHWH's teaching and leading, as did Ps. 25:4-5

The two added thoughts are the descriptive words about the one taught and led.

- sinners (BDB 308), Ps. 25:8

- humble (BDB 776), Ps. 25:9 (twice)

The paths of YHWH are characterized as

- lovingkindness (cf. Ps. 25:6,7; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: LOVINGKINDNESS)

- truth (cf. Ps. 25:5, see
SPECIAL TOPIC: AMEN)

25:10 ". . .testimonies" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS
FOR GOD'S REVELATION.

▣ "To those who keep His covenant" Notice the emphasis, not just on knowledge
(cf. Ps. 25:4-5) but obedience (cf. Deut. 5:10; 6:5; 7:9; 10:12; 11:1,13,22; 13:3; 19:9; 30:6,16,20;
Ps. 103:18). Obedience is not the mechanism of acceptance and forgiveness, which is the grace of YHWH,
but the result of meeting Him and being obedient to His will. Jesus said it so well in Luke 6:46, also
compare Eph. 2:8-9 and then Eph. 1:4; 2:10. Grace is always first! It is received by faith but it is a faith
that must be lived out (cf. James 2:14-26).

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

▣ "covenant" See
SPECIAL
TOPIC: COVENANT (ברית)

25:11 Any hope of forgiveness is based on the unchanging character of YHWH (cf. Ps. 102:26-27;
Malachi 3:6; James 1:17) and His Messiah (cf. Heb. 13:8). It is because of His name and character that
covenant sinners are restored to fellowship (cf. Ps. 79:9).

SPECIAL TOPIC:
CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

▣ "for it is great" Once we know the character of God (i.e., holiness, cf. Lev. 19:2;
Matt. 5:48) and the truth of God, our sins and their consequences become more evident to us. The tree of
the knowledge of good and evil (cf. Genesis 3) brought a revelation of our rebellion and its consequences
(cf. Galatians 3; book of Hebrews)!

12Who
is the man who fears the Lord?
He will instruct him in the way he
should choose.
13His
soul will abide in prosperity,
And

14The

And He will make them know His
covenant.

For He will pluck my feet out of the

25:12-15 As in strophes Ps. 25:4-7 and 8-11, the same themes continue here. Notice how the
faithful follower is characterized.

- he fears YHWH, Ps. 25:12,14, cf. Ps. 15:4; 103:11,13; 115:11; 118:4. see

SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR

- he knows YHWH's covenant, Ps. 25:14, see

SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW

- his eyes are continually toward YHWH, Ps. 25:15

Notice what YHWH will do for him.

- He will instruct him in the way, Ps. 25:12, cf. Ps. 16:11; 139:24

- He will provide good (BDB 373) for him and his descendants, Ps. 25:13

- He reveals to him His truths, Ps. 25:14

- He will keep his feet on the path and out of harm, Ps. 25:15

25:12 "choose" There is a theological balance in the Bible between the sovereign
acts of YHWH and His demand that humans choose Him and His ways (cf. Deut. 30:15,19; Josh. 24:14-15). We
are responsible for our choices!

SPECIAL
TOPIC: ELECTION/PREDESTINATION AND THE NEED FOR A THEOLOGICAL BALANCE

25:13 This describes the consequences of covenant disobedience (cf. Leviticus 26;
Deuteronomy 28; 30:15,19; Psalm 1; often called "The Two Ways").

25:14

The Hebrew word (BDB 691, KB 745) can mean (cf. Job 15:8; Ps. 111:1)

- confidential discussion – Job 29:4; Ps. 55:14

- secret counsel – Job 15:8; Prov. 11:13; 20:19; 25:9

- circle of confidants – Ps. 89:7; Jer. 15:17; 23:18,22

These connotations are fluid and interchangeable. There is a special consultation,
fellowship, and impartation of knowledge between the covenant God and His faithful followers.

25:15 As YHWH's eyes (see
SPECIAL TOPIC:
GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN) are continuously on those who fear Him and obey Him, so too,
the faithful continue to be faithful by keeping their full and focused
attention on Him (cf. Heb. 12:2)!

25:16-21 This strophe documents the psalmist's problems.

- I am lonely

- I am afflicted

- his heart has troubles (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: HEART)

- he is in distress

- his enemies are many

- they hate him with violent rage

- he fears shame

In light of these things he asks YHWH

- to turn to him (i.e., pay attention to him, cf. Ps. 69:16; 86:16)

- to be gracious to him

- to look upon/know his problems

- to forgive his sins (cf. Ps. 25:18; Ps. 32:1; 51:2; 103:3)

- to guard his soul (cf. Ps. 86:2; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: NEPHESH)

- to deliver him

His reasons for YHWH doing these things for him are

- he takes refuge in YHWH (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: REFUGE)

- he asserts either his or YHWH's integrity and uprightness (because of Ps. 25:18b it is best
to see these as characteristics of YHWH. AB (p. 159) suggests they are personified agents of YHWH)

- he waits for YHWH (cf. Ps. 25:3)

25:22 I think this is a separate closing statement (one verse beyond the acrostic pattern). The
King represents the people. This is the psalmist's final prayer request and it is national in scope.
Redeem (BDB 804, KB 911, Qal IMPERATIVE, see
SPECIAL
TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM) Your covenant people (i.e., "Israel"), for Your eternal
redemptive purposes (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- List the prayer requests of Ps. 25:4-7.

- List the psalmist's problem in Ps. 25:16-21.

- How would you summarize the message of this Psalm?

- How would you apply this Psalm to your life?
